issues.legal_issue: A mine owner may derive taxable annual net profits from mining when extracted ore is used to manufacture products that are sold, even if the ore itself is not sold.
material_facts: The companies held mines and extracted ore from them.
They used the extracted ore in their own manufacturing operations rather than selling it as ore.
They sold the finished products made using the ore.
The assessment treated the companies as having earned profits from their mining operations.
issues.conclusion: The profits attributable to the mining operation may be separated from the profits of the integrated manufacturing and selling activities and assessed as annual net profits from the mines.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 5, 6 and 72 of the Bengal Cess Act, 1880, as amended in Bihar, where a mine owner uses ore in further activities and sells the resulting product, the profit from mining may be embedded in the final realisation and apportioned. Kikabhai Premchand v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay was distinguished because the stock there was withdrawn without a sale or other commercial realisation; Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay v. Ahmedbhai Umarbhai & Co. and Anglo-French Textile Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Madras were relied on for the possibility of apportionment. Commissioner of Income-tax v. Dewan Bahadur S. L. Mathias and Commissioner of Income-tax v. Bai Shirinbai K. Kooka were considered.

rule.if: cess_assessment_appeal and mine_owner and extracted_ore_used_in_manufacturing and manufactured_product_sold

predicates.cess_assessment_appeal: The proceeding challenges an assessment of a local cess imposed by reference to profits from a mine.
predicates.mine_owner: The assessee held or owned the mine from which the material was extracted.
predicates.extracted_ore_used_in_manufacturing: The mine owner used the extracted ore in further manufacturing instead of selling it as ore.
predicates.manufactured_product_sold: The mine owner sold the product made using the extracted ore.

issues.definition: When a mine owner challenging a cess assessment uses extracted ore to make a product that is sold, the profit attributable to mining can be separately assessed.

issues.legal_issue: The absence of a specific statutory method for apportioning profits from an integrated mining and manufacturing operation does not make the cess charge unenforceable.
material_facts: The companies used extracted ore in further manufacturing and sold the resulting products.
The companies argued that the governing provisions did not specifically prescribe how to apportion profits in that situation.

The governing scheme provided for returns of annual net profits, permitted the assessing authority to ascertain profits where returns were missing or incorrect, and provided a valuation-based method if profits could not be ascertained.
issues.conclusion: The lack of a specific apportionment procedure for these circumstances does not prevent the cess from being imposed; the competent authorities must determine the mine profits, with the statutory fallback available where they cannot ascertain them.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 5, 6 and 72 of the Bengal Cess Act, 1880, as amended in Bihar, permit mine profits to be assessed even where the ore is transformed before sale. Section 75 authorizes the Collector to ascertain profits where a return is absent or incorrect, and section 76 provides a valuation-based fallback when annual net profits cannot be ascertained. The court held that no express, case-specific apportionment machinery was necessary to sustain the charge.

rule.if: cess_assessment_appeal and extracted_ore_used_in_manufacturing and manufactured_product_sold and assessing_authority_can_determine_mine_profits_or_use_fallback

predicates.cess_assessment_appeal: The proceeding challenges an assessment of a local cess imposed by reference to profits from a mine.
predicates.extracted_ore_used_in_manufacturing: The mine owner used the extracted ore in further manufacturing instead of selling it as ore.
predicates.manufactured_product_sold: The mine owner sold the product made using the extracted ore.
predicates.assessing_authority_can_determine_mine_p: The governing scheme allows the assessing authority to ascertain mine profits and provides a fallback method if it cannot do so.

issues.definition: In a cess-assessment appeal involving ore used to make a sold product, the absence of a specific apportionment method does not bar the cess if the assessing authority can determine mine profits or use a fallback.
